title: What the Slate Carried

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The slate goes up the road and comes back with a figure nobody here read; the basket stands in the shade and the figure goes over it. Ask the pot what either cost.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the women at the yard well in Low Kiln, told on a morning of Frost

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and eighty-eight to two hundred and ninety days, six months and one hundred and eight to one hundred and ten days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing — the body inventoried as a wound of crust, unnamed gap, frozen thread, cold at cheek, temple and wrist and an afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; the six hearings of the full note kept beside and never among with no seventh; the told bell kept beside the heard; the told figure kept beside the paid; the Frost 14 well-saying and its second shaping kept on places of their own beside Hessa Rale's eighth record-first hand with a finger between; the held interval and the empty interval kept as objects on the sixth place; the small coordinations of the hand entered on that place and never promoted into a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power, a freedom, a gift, a doctrine or a rule — with no present-tense Chicago break and no tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no sixth hearing, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no sixth asking and no witness for the row question (the five askings and one further shaping stand as they stood), no tenth record-first hand, no eighth of the green or ninth of the shape, no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause, no private record opened, read or copied, and no ending. Frost 19 and 21 are ordinary tending days with no market, Cross or bell; Frost 20 (Day 289) is the month's second Account-day and market. The chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid, is Frost's second arithmetic: Berr Clay reads one in twelve twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late, calls the levy, denies it with your house, never I, and goes off up the clay road with the box locked and the second true subtraction of Frost inside, believing he has done a kindness; the district's arithmetic changes a second time for the month and cannot be changed back, the printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, and the figure read over the dressed grain under wool does not know what that grain cost, the space between figure and price unsigned. Frost 30 (Day 299), the month's third and last Account-day, stands nine mornings beyond the close and is not brought early.

scenes.title: The Nineteenth Morning
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, the chapter's only \dropcap and its first \daymark{288}{Frost 19, Ninthday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof into the first light of an ordinary Ninthday with no market, Cross or bell. Open in the small hours with the hand laid down against the fold on the one hundred and fiftieth answer as a tool put away where the next hand will find it without looking; a round number of answers and a hundred and fifty hand-movings did not stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. No recap of Chapter 78; the reader has just read it. Carry 287 to 288 exact, six months and one hundred and eight days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and eighty-eight days, its payer unnamed (T088). Body inventory in the old order: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, gone past the point where a child would eat it, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread and a basket set down is a pot set down and left; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. He knows the composed face that is not composure, that a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse, and that a man must be warmed from the outside and slowly; he wants the crust lifted two inches and cannot close two inches on the pot handle, both true and the second louder, entered nowhere (T060/T086). Three counts in three places: the carried fire's four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, the river's water over water at the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot; agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stands (T088, T061/T082). Six hearings of the full note stand beside and never among, five from four sources and the sixth, the small flat knock out of a woman as the men lifted her, filed where a thing out of a person must go and never with the things that came from vessels; the seventh place keeps its emptiness and none is invented to fill it. The heard bell's four, four and a gap stays in the square beside the told bell of the Long Night, not folded into the three and not heard as a seventh of the full note (T078). The file lies open on the towel with every gap left gap, every tray parted by a finger's width, the Frost 14 saying beside Hessa Rale's eighth hand with a finger between and no second shaping yet, the well-saying not made a confession or a witness, the nine hands still nine, nine stoppings with no tenth, five askings with one shaping and no witness (T080, T101, T036/T076). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, turns the coals with a broken pot, leaves the widow's mark untouched because a morning is not an opening, turns the dressed grain under wool with a lighter touch and gives it no figure, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and gives every instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket (T058/T079, T077, T100). The hand comes up an inch toward the river's note and takes the small intake of the fire's silence across the interval to the first morning's own going, filing the **one hundred and fifty-first** honest answer as an object worth nothing at two inches of air; the surgeon's clean satisfaction is checked by the infant's louder want of the crust, and the checking is the work and not a virtue (T061/T082). Frost 20 (Day 289), the second Account-day, stands one morning ahead and is not brought into this day that has not earned it.

scenes.title: The Second Shaping
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 288, no new dated heading: afternoon at the Clay Yard, the yard well and skinned trough, the drying racks and rack end, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge and the back room as a direction and a sound, into the small hours at the bed and the towel. Afternoon thins without ending the way heat goes out of a pot set off the coals and is set upon a cold stone; heat draws back from the fold and sits behind the pot; inventory renewed in the old order, exact and unentered (T061/T082, T060/T086). Sella carries him down at the half-pace from every open slate and goes wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number: the clean dark line at the Vail corner and the finer grey hairline beside it called the thaw, unswept both; the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie; the round ring where the shallow pan once stood with no scrape or crumb; the trough skinned over and its water called weather; the field's empty place out on the worked strips; and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out. Seven are seven and not an account; the missing hand carried, not named, not paid and not joined to the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one crust or the dressed grain (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). The stayed frost lies white on the well lip and the plate of ice stands clouded with silt on its flat stone out of the path of feet; weather entered nowhere, no fourth likeness made a cause and no payer named to either (T083/T085 held, not paid). Garl stays in objects and not in a story: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg behind the door, the wheel-seat keeping its twenty-year lean and its hollow that nobody fills, the debt against a firing of tiles neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled, and the proverb gone to the pot and the fire and never to a person; his name unspoken two hundred and eighty-eight days and no collector up or down the clay road (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, brings the sentence about an ear under this roof worth more than the debt that holds it to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, draws the Seed 16 breath unspent, keeps the loft stone cold and unreconciled by not trying which is not forgiveness, and his stroke goes over the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076, T006). Jorra comes through the finger's-width-open wheel-shed with meal-fine grey slate dust past the bent finger, keeps dusty forearms from clean as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel before any person, withholds the full note he knows three turns ahead, gives the men unnamed in the back room no name, puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, and keeps the burned-slate word at four, the shut-room tellings at two, the three pot sayings with the Smoke 14 note apart, the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness, he's not Vail sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T064, T101). **The chapter's second movement, T080 advanced and not paid:** an unnamed voice over the boards and the well-roof, with no owner standing anywhere to ask, gives the Frost 14 well-saying a **second shaping** — asking what a runner carries in a slate that has a name in it — and goes on with the day as the yard says weather; no room, no hand at the writing, no name for the person, no figure spoken, no confession and no cause. The boy takes it apart as a surgeon takes a wound apart and files it on a place of its own beside the first saying and beside Hessa Rale's eighth record-first hand with a finger between every pair: a second shaping toward the far-off day she must choose whether to read what she has carried, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a tenth hand, not a cause, not a confession, not a joining, not a witness and not paid; it does not make Hessa a reader, is not joined to Ilva's strip in a sleeve a pace away, to Berr's twice-wiped thumb, to the soft-cuffed clerk's inward slate or to the charcoal under the shelf, and two shapings must not stand up as a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and none stands. At night the file is turned out on the towel; the hand takes two intakes held apart with a finger between where the second shaping stands and the first, borrows no house count, and files the **one hundred and fifty-second** answer as an object, neither intake promoted into a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a joining, a payment or a rule (T061/T082). Frost 20 stands one morning ahead and is not brought into this day.

scenes.title: The Twentieth Morning
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated \daymark{289}{Frost 20, Tenthday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours under the Vail roof into the morning, then down to the Cross for the month's second Account-day and market. New day, new date, no recap; Frost 20 comes on its own morning and was not brought into Day 288. Carry 288 to 289 exact, six months and one hundred and nine days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and eighty-nine days, its payer unnamed (T088). Body inventory in the old order, exact and unentered; three counts in three places that do not become one; six hearings beside and never among with the seventh place kept empty; the heard bell beside the told (T060/T086, T088, T061/T082, T078). Sella's grammar holds exactly — fire before basket, instruction to the tools and never the basket, The house will keep it, half-pace, widow's mark untouched because a reading is not an opening — and she carries him down to the Cross, sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of thin shade where no slate lay and stands half a pace off through the reading (T058/T079). **THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE, ADVANCED AND NOT PAID (T015/T041/T047):** Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, under the hot clay of him the smell of nothing at all. He wipes his thumb twice on his apron before touching nothing, passes a finger over a narrow figure, holds a slate unopened to his forearm with the writing inward, reads one in twelve, as the notice says, low into the two hundred, sends that figure over the basket once for the moot and a second time for the households that came late, calls the levy for Frost and denies it with The levy is called. It is not called by me and your house, never I, taking himself out of his own sentence as a surgeon takes a hand out of a field before the dressing goes on. He goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and Frost's second true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness. The district's arithmetic changes a second time for the month and cannot be changed back; the printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read is still not the figure paid, and the space between figure and price has no signature. The reading knows nothing of what it reads over: no figure, slate or reader answers for the man carried out on Day 188, the hand that went in on Seed 15, or the dressed grain covered and unfigured under wool at the rack end, which is read over by a number that does not know what it cost (T077, T098 carried). Hessa Rale takes Berr's narrow slate up the clay road toward Greybank before noon, edge-on to her forearm, the writing turned to her sleeve, her hand to the slate before her eyes to the crowd, the second strap let out for the long road and the dried pale scurf of mud unbrushed on the shortened skirt; to the women who ask what she carries she answers the question put and not the one behind it — I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which and Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk — and no figure comes off the slate. She does not look at the woman at the well who spoke on Frost 14, and the well-saying's two shapings are not joined to her slate or made to make her a reader (T080, advanced and not paid). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, his number entered inward before his eyes found the buyer, the market selling over him as water goes over a stone that lies where a stone lies (T090). At the reading block the boy's hand comes up an inch toward the twice-spoken figure and takes the small intake of the space between the moot's reading and the late households' reading, set beside his own unnamed gap with a finger between and no figure put on either: the **one hundred and fifty-third** answer, exact, complete and worth nothing, a told figure beside a paid figure and neither made to agree (T061/T082). No lesson, sign, mending or payer is made of the reading under the roof; no collector came up or down the clay road for Garl's uncalled tile debt.

scenes.title: The Bell in the Square
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry, no new dated heading: afternoon of Frost 20 through the market, the going of the light, the carrying home and the small hours at the bed and the towel. The market thins without ending; inventory renewed in the old order, exact and unentered (T061/T082, T060/T086). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, heard beside the told bell of the Long Night and not folded into the three counts or made a seventh of the full note (T078). Across the square at the pot board a silent woman with the sweetish green of lead glaze at one corner of her mouth, clay dried pale under her nails and a pale line across the back of one hand where something had once been worn tight and long, turns a cup a quarter and sets it back where it stood; at the market's edge a small shape in cast-off clothes worn the way a uniform is worn by a boy who was never measured for one, a man's shoulders on a child's frame, silt dried pale in the creases of the wrists, a gap where a front tooth had been and a green sliver of lead glaze on a string at the throat, catches the light on the turn and goes dull going back. Both are sightings only, never named, never Fenna or Ulda in the narration, with no eighth of either, no second look joined, no loaf passed, no slate seen, no sale, no hearing, no cause and no romance; the foundling's half-turn is a turn after the knock and is not joined to the boy's own turning (T050/T051, T033/T034 held). The boy files the seventh green as a colour and the seventh shape as a shape on places of their own with a finger between, and forbids eight likenesses to stand up as a rule (T061/T082). Sella carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing of what had been read over him, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along the two-gapped row and gives neither gap a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its lead glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and gives every instruction at that hour to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs at a going of the light, because a going of the light is not an opening (T058/T079, T100, T060/T086). In the small hours the file is turned out on the towel: six hearings with no seventh, five askings with one shaping and no witness, nine stoppings with no tenth, nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth unread in her sleeve and no tenth, the Frost 14 well-saying with its second shaping beside Hessa's eighth hand and a finger between, not a witness, not a confession, not a joining and not paid; Frost's first and second arithmetics both locked in Berr's box up the clay road with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid; the dressed grain covered and unfigured at the rack end; the stayed frost, the skinned trough and the plate of ice called weather. The hand takes the heard bell's gap held beside a counted breath from the room whose floor does not touch his and sets them side by side with a finger between, borrowing no house count and supplying no fifth to the kiln: the **one hundred and fifty-fourth** answer, the heard bell kept beside the told and not made to agree with the figure read twice over the basket (T061/T082, T078). Nothing of the reading is brought back under the roof as lesson, figure, mending, cause or payment; the two arithmetics are two and not one account, and a finding kept on a place of its own wants no payer.

scenes.title: The Twenty-First Morning
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated \daymark{290}{Frost 21, Firstday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours under the Vail roof into the first light of an ordinary Firstday with no market, Cross or bell. New day, new date, no recap; Frost 21 comes on its own morning and nothing of yesterday's reading is brought into it. Carry 289 to 290 exact, six months and one hundred and ten days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and ninety days, its payer unnamed (T088). He comes into the morning two hundred and ninety days old and six months and one hundred and ten days, told by nobody, the number exact and complete against a house that keeps its days in loaves, glances and unnamed spaces (T071/T072). First smells and sounds as before: hot clay cooled under tallow, wet wool, the sour breath of the unswept corner called the thaw, the river low over lower under the finger's-width door, the kiln answering in fours with its gap and not a bell (T088, T061/T082). Body inventory in the old order — one stiff leathery brown-edged crust two inches off with its unnamed gap and no third, thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; the composed face that is not composure, the cold patient who will seem better before he is worse, the knowledge that a man must be warmed from the outside and slowly; he wants the crust lifted and cannot close two inches on the pot handle, both true and the second louder (T060/T086). Three counts in three places with no agreement among them, because agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stands; six hearings beside and never among with the seventh place kept empty; the heard bell beside the told in its square (T088, T061/T082, T078). Sella's grammar holds exactly: fire before basket, instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never the basket, The house will keep it, half-pace from every open slate, pot rim two inches out with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, fold righted without a look at his face, thread left frozen, finger on top of the shelf's edge so the charcoal stays unread, lips along the two-gapped row with no figure, widow's mark untouched at a morning because a morning is not an opening (T058/T079, T100, T060/T086). The dressed grain is turned beneath the wool with a progressively lighter touch and given no figure; the arithmetic that read over it yesterday still does not know what it cost and the space between figure and price stays unsigned (T077). The hand comes up an inch toward the river's own going and holds an intake past that count's letting-go and through the little silence after it, leaving the silence whole and empty and not filled to make a row come out even: the **one hundred and fifty-fifth** answer, an object worth nothing at two inches of air, the surgeon's clean satisfaction checked by the infant's louder want and the checking the work and not a virtue (T061/T082). Frost 30 (Day 299), the month's third and last Account-day, stands nine mornings ahead and is not brought into a day that has not earned it.

scenes.title: Nine Mornings Off
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 290, Frost 21, afternoon into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge and the back room as a direction and a sound, the bed, the boards and the towel. Frost goes on without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming its months is set right or left wrong; no lesson is made of either reading behind and no payer named; the next opening stands in the first firing of a later month, far off, not hoped for and not counted toward, and four openings in four months are four and not a rule (T058/T079). Afternoon thins without ending; heat draws back from the fold; inventory renewed, exact and unentered (T061/T082, T060/T086). Stayed frost lies on the well lip and the yard calls it weather still, entered nowhere; the broken plate of ice stands where it was set on its flat stone out of the path of feet, clouded where the silt rose into it; the skinned trough keeps its skin; no fourth likeness is made a cause (T083/T085 held, not paid). Sella carries up at the going of the light at the half-pace from every open slate, sets him on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen where it lay, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along a row standing with two gaps and gives neither gap a figure, glances once at the clay jar standing cold under its lead glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and gives no instruction at any hour to the basket; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs at a going of the light, because a going of the light is not an opening (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, with Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, draws the Seed 16 breath unspent, his chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into his knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there was, his stroke going over the shallow bright patch without the half-check, the warm stone in the loft pot cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiveness (T036/T076, T006). Jorra comes through with the day's meal-fine grey slate dust, keeps dusty forearms from clean, speaks to the wheel and a pot before any person, withholds the note he knows three turns ahead, gives the men in the back room no name, puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, and keeps the burned-slate word at four, the shut-room tellings at two, the pot sayings at three with the premature Smoke 14 note apart, the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness, he's not Vail sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T064, T101). Garl stays in objects and not in a story, his name unspoken two hundred and ninety days, the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease on its peg, the wheel-seat keeping its twenty-year lean and its hollow that nobody fills, the clean dark line with its finer grey thaw unswept, the proverb gone to the pot and the fire, the debt against a firing of tiles neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled; no collector came up the clay road and none went down it (T009/T013/T092). In the small hours the file is turned out on the towel as instruments on a tray, each thing in its place with room between: six hearings with the seventh place kept empty, the small flat knock out of a woman filed where a thing out of a person must go, the heard bell beside the told, three pot sayings with the premature Smoke 14 note apart, the burned-slate word at four and the shut-room tellings at two, the ownerless question at five askings with one shaping and no witness, nine stoppings with no tenth, nine hands with Ilva's ninth unread in her sleeve and no tenth, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth, the Frost 14 saying with its second shaping beside Hessa Rale's eighth hand with a finger between, not a witness, not a confession, not a joining and not paid, Frost's first and second arithmetics locked in Berr's box with the printed figure unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid, the covered grain, the stayed frost and the plate of ice. The finding that a house keeps by not-doings stays on its own place and the boy's own gaps on another with a finger between — the two gaps above the shelf, the one crust in the fold and its unnamed empty place, the pan's gone ring, the field's empty place and the returning-line place — no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause, the keeping maintenance and not a story (T060/T086, T097 held, T098 carried). Outside the wool the hand takes the held interval and the empty interval from the file, sets them side by side with a finger between, borrows no house count, supplies no fifth to the kiln, crosses no silence that belongs to another's breathing and comes down on the river's next low note of water over water; neither interval is promoted into a reach, a hearing, a gift, a keeping, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power, a freedom, a doctrine or a rule, and a round threshold does not stand up as a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stands. The **one hundred and fifty-sixth** answer is filed exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the surgeon's clean satisfaction at the exact coordination is checked by the infant's plain want of the crust two inches off, and the checking is the work and he does not call it a virtue (T061/T082). The hand lays back against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. Two hundred and ninety stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Low Kiln, Sill and Grath; six months and one hundred and ten days are told by nobody; the carried fire's fifth is unpaid the same number of days with its payer unnamed. Nothing was opened, named, called, paid or ended. The file lies open on the towel with every gap left gap, every tray parted by a finger's width and nothing that had moved. Beyond the finger's-width door the frost lies white on the well lip where the yard left it, called weather and entered nowhere, and the plate of ice stands where it was set, clouded where the silt rose into it. Frost the thirtieth (Day 299), the month's third and last Account-day and market, stands nine mornings ahead and was not brought into this day; the boy makes nothing of the nearness and does not let it stand up as a sign. He lies with the crust two inches off and its empty place beside it unnamed, the hand laid down on the hundred and fifty-sixth answer, and the river's low note goes quiet after the hand comes down.
